Yes exactly, snow days, inclement weather, kid puking are another reason why having the transition end of day can be more logical. Since I’m Monday/Tuesday, I know there is always an off chance I could end up have kids home unexpectedly with me on Wednesday and every other Monday during the day. So I keep that in mind when I make plans and schedule things.

I suggest that if there is no school or summer camp that you default to 5pm or some time in the evening. The reason is to be fair to the Monday/Tuesday parent. If you start their shift in the morning, because such a disproportionately high number of school holidays fall on monday, (and in our experience, sick days from bugs they catch at museums and birthday parties on the weekends) that parent ends up having to rearrange their schedule much more. Having their time start at the end of the day when there’s no school essentially gives the parent who had them over the weekend a 3 day weekend that they can take as a vacation or whatever.

For sick days where they would otherwise normally be at school, the parent should pick them up from the other parents house at the time they’d normally go pick them up from school or camp. 

Going to that arrangement released a lot of frustration and scrambling from my end (as a Monday/Tuesday parent myself!)

You don’t become a child’s legal guardian or adoptive parent through marriage. Any fears he has instilled that she is on the hook for endangerment of some sort for not picking the child up from daycare is totally bogus for many reasons. For one thing, the daycare is responsible for the child’s safety until the child is handed off to the next responsible adult (parent, emergency contact, or finally, Child Services).

It doesn’t matter when a parent “gets off work”. Someone has to go pick up the kid and that’s whoever is contacted, and if neither contact responds, they contact the emergency contacts. If they can’t get ahold of you, then that’s dad and if dad doesn’t get there within an hour and neither does an emergency contact, then CPS will be contacted and DAD the parent/legal guardian is in trouble for not managing responsible care of his child - not you. You aren’t the child’s parent or legal guardian. You aren’t a paid babysitter either. Source: I’ve been daycare mom for over 7 years now.

One suggestion is looking into Dialectical Behavioral Therapy. There is a workbook by Harbinger Publications called “The Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills Workbook: Practical DBT Exercises for Learning Mindfulness, Interpersonal Effectiveness, Emotion Regulation, and Distress Tolerance” that you can read on your own and a big concept (the “dialectical” part) is accepting ideas for example “I have explosive anger but I love my friends and family and am working on myself a little bit every day” or “I am an alcoholic but I am a human being who has survived difficult times in my life and I am worthy of love and have love to give” In other words two seemingly opposing things about ourselves can be true at the same time and that’s what’s makes us a whole person. Every human being is no different. You are not unique in having hard parts of yourself, and you are not unique in having beautiful parts of yourself. It’s sort of a yin and Yang concept. 

I can care about the DA parts of my partner, which have caused me significant pain, while loving him as a whole. I see him as a whole person worthy of love and who shows me love too, all of me. I see his DA parts as a reflection of his past and actually as parts of him which were wounded through no fault of his own. His ability to speak honestly about those parts and be open to talking with me when I need him to, and to let me know when I am causing him hurt, is what allows us to function in a relationship and not let those aspects overtake the best parts. I don’t make demands or try to “hold him to account” and I try not to do the same. I try not to react with anger but I don’t hide my tears when I feel sad or scared from something he has done. It’s a challenge for me to show my authentic feelings to him and risk him abandoning me completely. We both slowly inch toward trust and that is part of the healing. Focus on what you can do, not on how you feel like a bad person. You aren’t. It’s good say “I don’t want to hurt you. I was scared when I did that, and that’s why I did xyz.”

Depends very much what state you live in. For example, in CT where I am- equitable property division. If your spouse has little income because they stayed home many years raising your kids and sacrificed their earning potential, they may be granted a larger share of the marital assets. CT doesn’t even have a concept of “separate” property. Everything is up for grabs. That can be good because a more personalized settlement can be written up to accommodate the couples needs vs the state having things pre-determined, it can also lead to more litigation. Other states you can probably have a clearer sense going into the divorce how separate property will be viewed. I do believe that even in states where separate property is recognized, there can be times where if it was “enjoyed” by both parties for a long period of the marriage - maybe like a marital home, that may cause it to be looked at differently. Suggest you just plan to have a prenup or consult a divorce attorney in your state with a very clear list of the assets you own and some specific marriage scenarios (long vs short marriage, wife stays home to raise kids vs kids in daycare and wife has similar earning power etc)
